subject: Fall 2020 School Reopening Plan
overview: District leadership presented the draft 2020-2021 reopening plan and responded to community questions regarding health protocols, instructional models, and facilities safety. The session focused on the transition to a hybrid learning model and the implementation of COVID-19 mitigation strategies prior to the state's submission deadline.

items.title: Reopening Pillars and Timeline
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent outlined the guiding pillars of equity, consistency, and safety, noting that a final plan must be submitted to the state by August 10.

items.title: Model Selection and Technology Access
items.summary: District officials stated that family decisions regarding hybrid or remote learning will likely be made on a semester basis, and the district is pursuing a one-to-one device distribution despite supply chain delays.

items.title: Health Safety, PPE, and Masking Requirements
items.summary: The district has secured over 21,000 masks and will provide face shields for teachers, while leadership is currently reconsidering the draft policy to require masks for kindergarten and first-grade students.

items.title: Special Education and English Learner Services
items.summary: High-needs special education students will be prioritized for in-person instruction and related services, while English Learner models will mirror mainstream schedules pending further state guidance.

items.title: Hybrid and Remote Instructional Models
items.summary: The hybrid model utilizes two cohorts attending in-person two days a week with remote Wednesdays, while the full remote option aims to mirror a typical school day with a mix of synchronous and asynchronous learning.

items.title: Collective Bargaining and Plan Finalization
items.summary: The administration confirmed that the current draft is approximately 80% complete and will undergo impact bargaining with the teachers' union throughout the week.

items.title: Facilities Maintenance and Ventilation
items.summary: The district is assessing HVAC filters and intends to run ventilation systems 23 hours a day to maximize air exchange in school buildings.

items.title: Logistics for Meals, Athletics, and Childcare
items.summary: Lunch will be served as grab-and-go meals in classrooms, while fall athletics are postponed until at least September 15 per state athletic association guidelines.

items.title: COVID-19 Screening and Response Protocols
items.summary: Daily temperature checks will not be conducted at school; families will instead be required to use a mobile symptom-tracking app before students arrive.

items.title: Professional Development and Staff Training
items.summary: The state has mandated 10 days of professional development before the school year begins, which the district will use to train all staff on remote instruction, safety, and trauma-informed care.
